words.definition: One of the main large land areas of the Earth.

contextSentences.en: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia.
The continent of Australia is sometimes referred to as Oceania when the Pacific islands are included.

words.example_en: We studied the concept of continent yesterday.

words.definition: A piece of land almost surrounded by water.

contextSentences.en: The Scandinavian peninsula stretches across Norway, Sweden, and the north of Finland.
The Korean peninsula is divided between North Korea in the north and South Korea in the south.

words.example_en: We studied the concept of peninsula yesterday.

words.definition: The imaginary line around the middle of the Earth.

contextSentences.en: Countries on the equator, such as Ecuador and Kenya, experience no distinct seasons.
The equator is approximately 40,075 kilometres long and is the longest line of latitude.

words.example_en: This experiment shows how equator works.
words.example_sk: Tento experiment ukazuje, ako funguje rovník.

words.definition: The distance north or south of the equator.

contextSentences.en: The 60th parallel north passes through cities such as Oslo, Helsinki, and St. Petersburg.
The higher the latitude, the farther a location is from the equator.

words.example_en: The latitude is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Zemepisná šírka je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: The distance east or west of the prime meridian.

contextSentences.en: Lines of longitude run from pole to pole and cross the equator at right angles.
A difference of 15 degrees of longitude corresponds to a time difference of one hour.

words.example_en: The longitude is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Zemepisná dĺžka je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: The usual weather conditions in a region over time.

contextSentences.en: The climate of a place is influenced by factors such as latitude, altitude, and ocean currents.
Continental climate, as found in Siberia, is characterised by very hot summers and extremely cold winters.

words.example_en: The climate is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Podnebie je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: A large slow-moving mass of ice on land.

contextSentences.en: Glaciers flow slowly downhill, shaped over thousands of years by the weight of the ice above.
The melting of glaciers contributes to rising sea levels and threatens coastal regions.

words.example_en: This experiment shows how glacier works.
words.example_sk: Tento experiment ukazuje, ako funguje ľadovec.

words.definition: A mountain that can erupt with lava and ash.

contextSentences.en: The eruption of Krakatoa in 1883 caused global temperatures to fall for several years.
Shield volcanoes like those in Hawaii have broad, flat shapes and produce relatively gentle eruptions.

words.definition: A low area of land between hills or mountains.

contextSentences.en: The Nile Valley in Egypt was the foundation of ancient Egyptian civilisation thanks to its fertile soil.
U-shaped valleys are formed by glaciers, while V-shaped valleys are carved by rivers.

words.example_en: The teacher explained the term valley.

words.definition: A large flat area of land that is higher than the land around it.

contextSentences.en: The Anatolian plateau in Turkey lies at an average altitude of about 1,000 metres.
On the Altiplano plateau in South America lies Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world.

words.example_en: The plateau is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Náhorná plošina je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: An area of land formed at the mouth of a river.

contextSentences.en: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is the largest delta in the world, spanning Bangladesh and India.
Deltas are extremely fertile but are vulnerable to flooding and rising sea levels.

words.example_en: The delta is important in this field.
words.example_sk: Delta je v tejto oblasti dôležitý.

words.definition: The outline of a coast as seen on a map.

contextSentences.en: Norway's coastline is shaped by deep fjords formed by glacial movement during the last Ice Age.
Mangroves along tropical coastlines protect against storm surges and support rich marine habitats.

words.definition: A very dry area of land with little vegetation.

contextSentences.en: The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest place on Earth – in some parts it never rains.
Deserts cover about one third of the Earth's land surface and form in areas with very little rainfall.

words.example_en: We studied the concept of desert yesterday.

words.definition: The number of people living in a place.

contextSentences.en: Asia is home to more than half of the world's total population.
An ageing population poses major challenges for social welfare systems in many industrialised countries.

words.definition: One half of the Earth divided by the equator or a meridian.

contextSentences.en: In the Southern Hemisphere, seasons are reversed – it is summer in December and winter in June.
The Western Hemisphere includes North and South America as well as parts of Europe and Africa.

words.example_en: The teacher explained the term hemisphere.
